response.text:
Recent work supports evaluating explanations through ranking changes rather than sensitivity alone. [TRACE (RecSys 2026)](https://github.com/devUuung/TRACE) provides targeted, ranking-aware counterfactual explanations for sequential recommendation, including GRU4Rec support. [TimeSHAP (KDD 2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073), an earlier methodological foundation, attributes recurrent predictions to events/features and groups older history through temporal coalition pruning. Its findings concern a fraud-detection GRU; they do not establish that older interactions are unimportant in recommendation. [RSS (2025 journal publication)](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/299238/) studies recency-aware training sampling across GRU4Rec and other backbones, providing motivation to investigate temporal reliance separately from explanation faithfulness.

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: pair each unchanged validation history with deletion of equally sized recent versus older blocks; compact retained events and restore left padding. Test order separately through length-preserving shuffles, including a shuffle that preserves the final item. Keep targets and candidate sets fixed; report signed target-rank deterioration, HR@10 changes, and paired uncertainty by category. Greater deterioration after recent-block deletion supports useful recent-context dependence; large score movement without ranking benefit establishes sensitivity only. Compare event attribution against matched random deletion and inspect how input influence reaches the final GRU state. Gate values or hidden-state similarity alone cannot establish faithful attribution or harmful forgetting. Read the final nonpadding position, never count−1. These interventions diagnose the fitted model under altered histories; they do not identify users’ true intentions.
